name: RabbitMQ
description: RabbitMQ broker reads over the management HTTP API: cluster overview, node health, the vhost list, and per-queue, per-exchange and per-connection state. Read-only; no queue, exchange, binding, vhost, user or policy write, and no publish/get/purge, is wired here.

tools.name: overview
tools.description: Get the broker overview: RabbitMQ and Erlang versions, cluster name, total object and message counts, and the global message rates

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description: List the cluster nodes with their running state, memory and disk alarms, and file-descriptor and socket usage

tools.name: list_vhosts
tools.description: List the virtual hosts with their message counts and message rates

tools.name: list_queues
tools.description: List queues with their vhost, node, durability, consumer count and ready/unacknowledged message depth

name.description: Optional case-sensitive substring to filter queue names by

tools.name: list_exchanges
tools.description: List exchanges with their vhost, type (direct/fanout/topic/headers), durability and internal flag

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List client connections with their peer host, protocol, authenticated user, vhost, channel count and connection state

tools.name: healthchecks_alarms
tools.description: Check whether any resource alarm (memory or disk) is in effect across the cluster; returns ok or a failure reason

needs_review: READ-ONLY by design: all seven tools are GET and carry write:false. The management API's mutating surface (PUT /api/queues, /api/exchanges, /api/vhosts, /api/users, /api/policies; DELETE of the same; POST /api/exchanges/.../publish and /api/queues/.../get, which publishes and destructively consumes) is deliberately not modelled.

list_queues sends disable_stats=false so message depths are populated; on a very large broker the management API can be slow to assemble per-object stats, which is why page_size is exposed and defaulted to 100. The pick keeps the paginated envelope (page/page_count/total_count) plus items[].

list_nodes / list_vhosts / list_exchanges / list_connections return a BARE JSON ARRAY, so the pick uses the '[]' whole-response array form. On a fresh broker list_connections is a 200 with an empty array (no clients yet), which is the honest expected live result, not an error.

message_stats and rate fields appear on overview only once the management stats database has collected a sample; immediately after boot they may be absent, so the pick tolerates their absence rather than requiring them.

LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: every tool carries a tool-level _probe. The four bare-array listers and overview/healthchecks take no input, so their _probe is deliberately EMPTY ({}). list_queues probes page 1 / page_size 100. No credential is ever hinted. Proven against docker rabbitmq:3-management with a purpose-set user, then destroyed.

healthchecks_alarms returns HTTP 200 with {status:ok} when no alarm is set and HTTP 503 with {status:failed,reason} when one is. The live harness requires 2xx, so this tool proves the healthy path; the 503-with-body case is a documented runtime behaviour the harness cannot assert here.
rateLimit 30/min is a local courtesy and spend guard, not a RabbitMQ number: the management API enforces no request rate limit of its own.
